thread:
eve (Customer): hey, we're suddenly getting a lot of 429s after switching to rwd-large-64k. started around 08:15 UTC. no code changes otherwise.

sam (Support): sorry to hear that — can you share a sample request + headers (remove API key) and any Request-Id from response headers? also did you change request pattern or fanout?

Eve (Customer): sending curl now. we're hitting the API from a prefetcher that fans out ~8 requests per user to gather context. payload is big (~40k tokens). here's a redacted curl:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-64k","input":"<huge_context>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

Eve (Customer): sample response headers: `x-rwd-request-id: rq_3Yk2...` `x-rwd-rate-limit-model: 300rpm/6000tpm` `retry-after: 1` and body `{"error":"Too Many Requests"}`

sam (Support): thanks. quick notes: the `x-rwd-rate-limit-model` is helpful — rwd-large-64k has a lower effective RPM for large-context streaming due to longer token processing time and concurrency ceilings.

linda (Runtime Eng): adding context from runtime: for rwd-large-64k we apply adaptive throttling when requests exceed concurrency or when long-context tokens in flight push CPU/GPU queues high. nominal public cap = 300 RPM and 60 concurrent requests per account for that model, but effective throughput drops with ~40k+ contexts because each request holds GPU slots longer.

linda (Runtime Eng): reproduction note: fanout of 8 * concurrent users * 40k context => queueing. that can surface as 429s even if RPM looks under the nominal cap because TPM and concurrency are the gating factors.

sam (Support): recommended immediate mitigations: 1) reduce prefetch fanout to 2-3, 2) request smaller context slices and stitch client-side, 3) add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (start 500ms -> 2s -> 5s), 4) consider using rwd-std-32k for prefetch + upgrade to dedicated for sustained high throughput.

Eve (Customer): do you have exact numbers we can use to tune prefetch? e.g., acceptable fanout per 40k context to avoid 429s?

linda (Runtime Eng): rough safe starting point: with 40k contexts, try <= 8 RPM per concurrent pipeline worker and fanout <= 2, target concurrency per account <= 12. If you need sustained bigger fanout, Dedicated capacity or rate increase is the right path.

sam (Support): also check billing/auth side: we saw cases where newly rotated API keys briefly hit auth validation paths causing small auth latency spikes that amplify queueing — do you see any `401` or `403` interleaved?

Eve (Customer): only 429s and occasionally `retry-after: 1`. no auth errors.

sam (Support): ok. we'll open an internal trace for `rq_3Yk2...` to check where throttles fired. @infra-bot kicking off a trace search now. :mag:

infra-bot: trace job created for request_id=rq_3Yk2..., window=2026-02-10T08:10:00Z..2026-02-10T08:25:00Z. assigned to eng-runtime queue #142.

linda (Runtime Eng): one more tip: enable streaming and send smaller initial tokens to accept partial prefixes; streaming reduces peak KV cache pressure. also enable client-side token accounting and stop sending N extra tokens in prefetch.

Eve (Customer): thanks — we'll throttle fanout and add backoff. please update when trace completes.

sam (Support): will do. follow-up: if you want immediate throughput guarantees we can discuss a short Dedicated trial to validate target TPS with 40k contexts.

Eve (Customer): interested, please DM next steps. :thumbsup:

sam (Support): noted — DM incoming. last update: trace job queued, we expect timeline ~4-8h. we will post results in this thread.
